chapters.title: I See What You're Thinking
chapters.sourcePressure: The opening promise must show that nonverbal behavior can expose comfort, discomfort, interest, hesitation, and direction before speech has fully edited the moment, while explicitly avoiding mind-reading claims.
chapters.coreMove: Notice the split between polished words and whole-body behavior, then use the split to become more curious rather than more certain.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would present body language as mind reading or as a way to decode hidden thoughts from a single visible cue.

chapters.title: Mastering the Secrets of Nonverbal Communication
chapters.sourcePressure: This method chapter must teach responsible reading through context, baseline, clusters, comfort versus discomfort, and restraint around isolated cues.
chapters.coreMove: Build a reading method: establish baseline, watch for clusters, and keep each cue inside the situation that produced it.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would list nonverbal tricks and make the chapter sound like a shortcut manual for instant interpretation.

chapters.title: Living Our Limbic Legacy
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter may use limbic framing only narrowly: fast protective response, orientation, comfort, discomfort, and recovery, without precise unsupported neuroscience.
chapters.coreMove: Read early body reactions as protective timing signals, then slow interpretation until recovery and context show more.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would claim the limbic system always tells the truth or that biological reaction reveals exact motive.

chapters.title: Getting a Leg Up on Body Language
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter must make feet and legs specific: direction, readiness, withdrawal, blocking, stillness, fidgeting, and limits from room layout, injury, habit, temperature, footwear, and context.
chapters.coreMove: Use feet and legs to read where movement energy is going before the face or words admit it.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would say pointed feet always reveal desire to leave or attraction, ignoring setting and physical constraints.

chapters.title: Torso Tips
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter must focus on torso, hips, chest, and shoulders as signals of openness, protection, comfort, discomfort, and territorial tension.
chapters.coreMove: Read torso orientation and shielding as evidence of how open or protected the person is becoming in the moment.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would turn posture into confidence advice or claim that a turned torso proves dislike, dominance, or deceit.

chapters.title: Knowledge Within Reach
chapters.sourcePressure: The arms chapter has thinner support, so it must stay concrete: barriers, reach, tucked arms, folded arms, protective holding, invitation, restraint, and distance management.
chapters.coreMove: Watch how the arms manage distance: what they block, protect, offer, contain, or reach toward.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would treat folded arms as automatic defensiveness or make arms a generic signal of attitude.

chapters.title: Getting a Grip
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter must use hands and fingers as visible surfaces for confidence, stress regulation, soothing, emphasis, restraint, hidden hands, palms, finger interlacing, and rubbing.
chapters.coreMove: Read the hands as active regulators and communicators: what they show, hide, tighten, soothe, or release.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would claim open palms prove honesty or hand tension proves deceit, dominance, or fear.

chapters.title: The Mind's Canvas
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter must handle the face as expressive but socially managed, using smiles, lips, eyebrows, eyelids, jaw tension, gaze limits, timing, mismatch, and whole-body context.
chapters.coreMove: Treat the face as a managed display that becomes useful only when timing and the rest of the body give it weight.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would sell micro-expression certainty, eye-contact honesty myths, or face-only verdicts.

chapters.title: Detecting Deception
chapters.sourcePressure: This chapter must be the strongest caution point: pressure, inconsistency, pacifying, topic-linked change, baseline, clusters, and verification can guide inquiry but cannot prove deceit.
chapters.coreMove: When deception is possible, use nonverbal changes to locate pressure points and verification needs, not to declare a lie.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would make the chapter a lie-detection checklist where stress or fidgeting exposes guilt.

chapters.title: Some Final Thoughts
chapters.sourcePressure: The conclusion has thin direct support, so it must synthesize prior lessons: whole-body observation, context, restraint, pattern, timing, self-observation, and practical next moves.
chapters.coreMove: Turn the full method into a repeatable practice: observe the whole body, compare context, check yourself, and choose the next move with restraint.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would invent a new final framework or end with generic confidence and relationship advice.
